newsitem.title: UK: Principal Healthcare to buy Quality Care.
newsitem.headline: Principal Healthcare to buy Quality Care.

text.p: Britain's Principal Healthcare Plc said on Monday it would buy Quality Care Homes Plc in an agreed bid worth about 46.3 million stg.
The bid valued each Quality Care share at 330p, the companies said in a joint statement.
Principal said shareholders with about 50.9 percent of Quality Care's shares had agreed to accept its offer.
The company said Quality Care shareholders would be able to choose to receive a partial loan note alternative instead of cash.
Quality Care's shares closed at 317.5p on Friday.
Principal said the deal would enable it to expand its portfolio of nursing homes in Britain.
Quality Care's chairman, Duncan Bannatyne, said he would be leaving the company, but added that he believed the offer represented a good deal for shareholders.
Principal Healthcare is a unit of Principal Healthcare Finance, which is majority owned by U.S. group Omega Healthcare Investors Inc.
Principal said Termrate Ltd, its joint venture with Tamaris Plc, would operate Quality Care's portfolio of homes after the deal.
